messages:
alice-nguyen: heads up — proposing a lightweight sampling-based QA layer for low-bit rollouts (FP8/INT8/4-bit). goal: detect quality drift early without full-suite evals.
ben-choi: sounds useful. how lightweight? what's the expected perf hit?
alice-nguyen: target <2% extra latency on offline evals. sampling only 0.5-2% of live traffic for runtime checks; offline daily sweep uses 5% of stored traces.
carol-perez: we should do stratified sampling (prompt buckets + tail-token emphasis). distribution skews wildly across customers.
dmitri-ivanov: agree — also add prompt-aware weighting so high-cost customers get higher sampling. runtime constraints: need to avoid adding KV pressure.
eva-mlops: telemetry-wise we want these signals: token-level perplexity delta, ngram BLEU-like regression, output-embedding cosine drift, and hallucination spike rate. keep them per-model+profile.
ben-choi: what's the detection threshold? false positives are costly (unnecessary rollback).
alice-nguyen: proposal: two-stage thresholds — soft alarm (early warning) at 2 sigma, hard alarm triggers rollback at 4 sigma relative to baseline. baseline = weekly rolling median from golden-run.
dmitri-ivanov: sketching config (example):
```
q_validation:
  sampling_rate: 0.01   # 1% of requests
  stratified: true
  weights:
    enterprise: 5
    standard: 1
  metrics:
    - name: token_cosine_drift
      soft_threshold: 1.2
      hard_threshold: 1.6
    - name: perplexity_ratio
      soft_threshold: 1.15
      hard_threshold: 1.4
  cooldown_minutes: 30
  rollback_on_hard: true
```

eva-mlops: looks good. add a TTL for sample traces (14d) and a privacy scrub step before storage. also tie alerts into paging with runbook links.
carol-perez: for offline calibration sweeps, we should run calibration-only passes (no retrain) on a holdout that emphasises numeric stability — e.g., extremes of token lengths and prompts with many numbers.
ben-choi: who owns the initial thresholds? ML team or SRE? we need an on-call-friendly owner.
alice-nguyen: ML owns tuning thresholds, SRE owns runtime enforcement and paging. we'll document in runbook.
deployment-bot: Canary started for model redwood/v3-int4-sparse (profile: aggressive-compress). 100 reqs sampled.
ben-choi: nice. after 1h we should evaluate both soft and hard metrics. can we get a dashboard tile?
eva-mlops: I'll add a dashboard and a daily digest email for the ML leads.
dmitri-ivanov: runtime optimization: do expensive metrics async with a best-effort path. quick proxy metrics (embed cosine via reduced-dim sketch) for hot path.
carol-perez: don't forget calibration drift detection across quantization scales (e.g., FP8 dynamic range compression). the same sampling should include per-layer activation histograms.
alice-nguyen: action items: @dmitri-ivanov prototype config + async proxy; @eva-mlops dashboard+alert; @carol-perez define stratified buckets and calibration holdouts; @ben-choi run initial canary and post results in 1h. I'll draft runbook.
dmitri-ivanov: will prototype today. expect a perf note + PR.
eva-mlops: will add dashboard card and alert rules.
ben-choi: running initial evaluation now.
alice-nguyen: cool — if anything hits hard threshold, auto-rollback enabled. otherwise we'll use soft alarms for manual triage. :eyes:
carol-perez: also recommend periodic calibration audits (weekly) and a monthly sample full-eval to catch slow degradations.
alice-nguyen: thanks all. logging decisions to the RFC follow-up doc and linking runbook. will update thread when PR merges. :thumbsup:
